blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A notifier picks a channel with `if (n instanceof Alert) pager(n); else if (n instanceof Message) email(n); else if (n instanceof UrgentAlert) pagerAndCall(n); else log.debug("unknown");`, where `UrgentAlert extends Alert`. The build uses `javac -Xlint:all`. What happens with an `UrgentAlert`?

options.text: The chain compiles, and an UrgentAlert is only paged, since the Alert test is true for it and is tried first
options.says: an if chain runs its tests in order and javac doesn't judge their order, so the subclass branch can never run and nothing warns

options.text: The chain compiles, and an UrgentAlert is paged and called, since instanceof tests match the most specific class first
options.says: the tests run in the order they are written; the first one that is true wins

options.text: javac rejects the chain, since a test that an earlier test always wins is an error, as in a switch
options.says: javac rejects a dominated case label in a switch, but it doesn't check the order of if tests

options.text: javac warns about the chain, since a test that an earlier test always wins is flagged as dead code
options.says: -Xlint:all is silent about the order of instanceof tests in an if chain

origin.section: An instanceof Chain Fails Silently on a Subclass or a New Type; an Abstract Method Makes the Compiler Ask

questions.stem: A `Renderer` interface declares `default String render(Node n) { return "<!-- unsupported -->"; }` plus abstract `render(Heading h)` and `render(Table t)`. The abstract class `Node` has one method, `String accept(Renderer r) { return r.render(this); }`, and `Heading` and `Table` extend `Node` without declaring anything. What does `new Heading().accept(htmlRenderer)` return?

options.text: The Heading output, since `this` refers to a Heading object while accept runs
options.says: the overload was chosen when Node was compiled, from the declared type of this there, which is Node

options.text: The unsupported comment, since `render` was chosen where `this` is declared as a Node
options.says: an overload is fixed at compile time from the argument's declared type; inside Node, this is a Node, so render(Node) runs for every subclass

options.text: The Heading output, since the JVM picks the overload from the argument's run-time class
options.says: the run-time choice looks only at the receiver, here the renderer; the argument's class plays no part

options.text: The unsupported comment, since a default method is chosen before the class's own overloads
options.says: the default runs here because it is the overload chosen for a Node argument, not because defaults come first

origin.section: Spot the Problem: the accept Methods Look Duplicated

questions.stem: `static void broadcast(List<Subscriber> subs, Event e)` only loops over `subs` and calls `s.notify(e)`. A caller holds a `List<EmailSubscriber>`, and `EmailSubscriber implements Subscriber`. Which parameter type lets that caller pass its list, and what does it change inside `broadcast`?

options.text: `List<? extends Subscriber>`; the method still reads each element as a Subscriber but can't add one
options.says: ? extends accepts a list of any subtype and gives elements back as Subscriber; the list could hold any subtype, so the compiler refuses add

options.text: `List<? super Subscriber>`; the method still reads each element as a Subscriber but can't add one
options.says: ? super Subscriber accepts only lists of Subscriber or its supertypes, not List<EmailSubscriber>, and its elements come out as Object

options.text: `List<? extends Subscriber>`; the method can add any Subscriber but reads elements back as Object
options.says: that describes ? super; with ? extends, reads give Subscriber and add takes only null

options.text: `List<? super Subscriber>`; the method can add any Subscriber but reads elements back as Object
options.says: true of ? super Subscriber, but such a parameter doesn't accept a List<EmailSubscriber>

origin.section: A List of Parcels Is Not a List of Shipments; a Wildcard Says Whether the Method Reads or Writes

questions.stem: A pricing loop calls `rule.apply(order)` hundreds of millions of times an hour, and each `apply` is a few arithmetic operations. With one `Rule` class in production, HotSpot inlined `apply` into the loop. A release adds two more `Rule` classes, and orders now reach all three in roughly equal shares. What happens to that call?

options.text: It stays inlined, since HotSpot inlines calls to whatever classes the call-site profile shows
options.says: the page's run shows C2 inlining one or two classes and compiling a virtual call for three or four

options.text: It stays compiled the same way, since a third class in the call-site profile changes nothing for an interface call
options.says: with one class the call was inlined; with three it becomes a real virtual call, so the compiled code changes

options.text: It stops being inlined, since a third class in the call-site profile is one more than HotSpot inlines
options.says: the JIT records the classes reaching each call site; with three or more in equal shares it compiles a virtual call and inlines nothing, which can matter in a loop this hot with bodies this small

options.text: It stops being compiled, since HotSpot interprets calls to whatever classes the call-site profile shows
options.says: the call site is still compiled by C2, as a virtual call

origin.section: A Call Site That Has Seen Three Classes Isn't Inlined, Which Matters Only in a Hot Loop

concepts: An instanceof chain runs its tests in order without any compiler check, so an early superclass test hides a subclass's branch and a new type falls into the default.
A List<Parcel> is not a List<Shipment>; a parameter read from is ? extends T and one written to is ? super T, each giving up the other direction, while arrays convert and fail at run time instead.
HotSpot inlines a call site that has seen one or two classes and compiles a virtual call once three or more reach it; the cost matters only for tiny methods in hot loops and is to be measured.
